query: Can GPG be made to prefer a PGP smartcard when present while still falling back to the on-disk private key when it isn't?
reference_answer: GPG determines whether to use a smartcard based on whether the key record indicates the key is stored on the card. If the full private key exists locally, GPG will not default to the card. There's no built-in way to force GPG to prefer the card while keeping the local key present. A common workaround is to move the full private key to a separate GnuPG home directory and use the keytocard command to store the key on the card in the main directory. You can switch between key storage locations by changing the GNUPGHOME environment variable as needed.
thread_title: How to force GPG to use a Keycard when it is available

query: What hardware, if any, can a user-mode process access directly without going through system calls?
reference_answer: User-mode processes cannot directly access hardware devices without system calls. While they may interact with device memory mapped into user space, actual communication with the hardware requires kernel involvement through system calls. This restriction is enforced by the CPU and applies across operating systems to maintain security and stability.
